items.title: [Bugfix] Keep GEMM workspace addresses stable once CUDA graphs may have captured them
items.body:
Related: #52540, #34948

## Purpose

Root-cause fix-out for the SM120 NVFP4 serving crashes in #52540 (and at least some reports in #34948): a **shared GEMM workspace that changes device address after CUDA graphs have captured launches against it** turns every subsequent replay into a use-after-free.

The defect that kills the #52540 configuration lives in FlashInfer: every cuDNN GEMM execute path in `flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py` grows its shared 32 MiB workspace with `tensor.resize_()` when an execution plan asks for more. `resize_()` frees the old storage and moves the buffer; launches already enqueued, and CUDA graphs captured earlier, keep dereferencing the old address, which the caching allocator immediately reuses for unrelated tensors. Fix filed upstream as flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4553. Instrumented evidence from the failing machine (full matrix in #52540):

```
Capturing CUDA graphs (mixed prefill-decode, PIECEWISE):  89%|████████▉ | 8/9
[F5WS 21:32:46] RESIZE old_ptr=0x7efadc000000 old=33554432 new=33554688
[F5WS 21:32:46] RESIZE done new_ptr=0x7efa8d200000
```

One cuDNN FP8 plan wanted 256 bytes more than the 32 MiB default, mid-capture; the eight piecewise graphs already captured kept the stale pointer, and the server died minutes into serving — a GPU coredump caught `cudnn_generated_fort_native_*` faulting on a "pointer" that was two int32s of unrelated tensor data (`0x27000013FF`).

This PR does two things on the vLLM side:

1. **Pre-grow FlashInfer's shared FP8 GEMM workspace during kernel warmup, before any capture** (`presize_flashinfer_gemm_workspaces` in `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`, called from `kernel_warmup`). With the address fixed at its high-water mark before the first capture, the in-place grow in current FlashInfer releases never fires. This is a guard, not the root fix; it is cheap (one 64 MiB buffer per device on the FlashInfer FP8 path), and it protects every vLLM+FlashInfer user until a FlashInfer release carries flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4553.

2. **Fix the same defect class in vLLM's own tree**: `SM100Workspace.ensure_size` in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/cutlass_mla.py` grew its shared workspace with `resize_()` too. Growth now allocates a fresh buffer and retires the old one instead of freeing it, so graphs captured against an older generation keep a live, correct address (their capture-time size was sufficient for the shapes baked into them).

## Diagnosis trail (short form; full evidence in #52540)

- Same model FP8-quantized end-to-end: stable 35 h. NVFP4-mixed build: dies/wedges in ~16.5 min under 24-way load, graphs ON. Established by falsification: not the NVFP4 GEMM kernels (swapping/removing them changes nothing), not KV shape, not MTP/prefix-cache.
- GPU coredump-on-exception on the failing config names the faulting kernel: a cuDNN FP8 GEMM (`matMul_pointwise_pointwise`) reading garbage pointer arguments — the FP8 projections feeding the GDN/attention layers, not the NVFP4 GEMMs themselves.
- Instrumenting FlashInfer's eight `resize_` sites shows the workspace moving *during* vLLM's piecewise capture on this build; the FP8-only build happens to hit its workspace high-water mark before capture, which is why it never crashed. The quantization scheme was never the mechanism — it only determined *when* the first oversized cuDNN plan arrived.
- Instrumenting further under `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` attributed the *hang* mode to the same lane: the failure surfaces in seconds as CUDA error 702 raised through `execute_cudnn_gemm_fp8_graph → execute_plan_at_index`. cuDNN split-K plans keep completion semaphores inside the workspace (the observed oversized request is exactly 32 MiB + 256 B); a workspace whose memory is not zeroed — freed-and-reused after the in-place resize, or a recycled dirty allocator block — makes the GEMM kernel spin forever on a garbage semaphore word. Hence the second commit of flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4553 and the `zero_init=True` in this PR's pre-size guard.
- With the complete FlashInfer fix (stable address + zeroed replacement) bind-mounted: the launch-blocking configuration that previously failed in 45 s ran a clean 15-minute probe, and a full-speed soak at 3.3x the baseline MTTF is documented in #52540 (final numbers there). 50 temperature-0 classification goldens are byte-identical across the change.

## Test Plan

- `presize_flashinfer_gemm_workspaces`: exercised on 2× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) with the #52540 reproducer; no behavioural change beyond the pre-allocation.
- `cutlass_mla.py`: mechanical change, growth path preserved; covered by existing CUTLASS MLA tests on SM100.

## Test Result

See validation numbers above; goldens byte-identical.

items.title: [BugFix] lora_base_layer / routed_experts order in expert param mapping
items.body:
## Purpose

Follow up of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/31104 as broken by refactor at https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41184

In RoutedExperts.build_expert_params_mapping the LoRA base-layer prefix was concatenated AFTER routed_experts_prefix, producing ``experts.routed_experts.base_layer.w13_``. The live LoRA parameter tree is nested the other way — ``experts.base_layer.routed_experts.w13_weight`` — so strict loaders (DeepseekV2/DSV3/...) that do ``params_dict[name_mapped]`` with this ``param_name`` raise KeyError on every routed-expert weight sync.

Swap the concatenation order to ``{lora_base_layer_prefix}{routed_experts_prefix}`` so ``param_name`` becomes ``experts.base_layer.routed_experts.w13_`` and the ``params_dict`` lookup hits.

## Test Plan

Test with verl LoRA merge = False with Moonlight 16B

## Test Result

End to end weight sync passes.

items.title: [Bug]: Qwen3.6-27B (dense Gated-DeltaNet) permanently hard-wedges the V1 engine — two reproducible modes (2 large images; long multi-turn text), possibly related
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64), glibc 2.35 Python: 3.12.13 | platform Linux-6.17.0-1026-nvidia-x86_64 PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130 (CUDA build 13.0) vLLM Version: 0.23.0 CUDA available: True | CUDA runtime 13.0.88 | driver 595.71.05 GPU: 8× NVIDIA B200 [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.12 [pip3] transformers==5.12.0 [pip3] triton==3.6.0 env: VLLM_USAGE_SOURCE=production-docker-image, VLLM_ENABLE_CUDA_COMPATIBILITY=0, TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.5 8.0 8.6 8.9 9.0 10.0 12.0+PTX ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary vLLM **0.23.0**, **Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B** (dense FullAttn + Gated-DeltaNet), single GPU TP=1, `--attention-config TRITON_ATTN`, `--max-model-len 262144`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `mamba_cache_mode=align`. The engine **permanently hard-wedges** (generation stops, `/health` still 200, only restart recovers) in two reproducible cases: - **Mode A** — a request with **two large images** → **fixed** by raising `--max-num-batched-tokens` 8192→32768. - **Mode B** — concurrent **long multi-turn (~180k-token) prefills** → **not** fixed by `--max-num-batched-tokens`. Reported together because both wedge the same GDN model and **we can't tell if it's one bug or two** (stacks and fix-behavior differ). Related to #40707 / #47738 (both env 0.18–0.23). ## Mode A — 2 large images (scheduler-admission wedge) Each request has **two distinct 3024×4032 images** (11,844 vision tokens each). At `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` it wedges on the first batch: `running=1, waiting=11`, gen frozen, KV≈0.9%. py-spy MainThread is **idle in the scheduler** (`_process_engine_step`), admitting none. Single-variable bisection: **8192 → WEDGE, 32768 → CLEAN** (65 completed); `--max-num-seqs` 64/384 and `--mm-processor-cache-gb` 256/0 make no difference (still WEDGE). > **Our workaround (works for us):** setting **`--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`** eliminates Mode A entirely — the multimodal load that reliably wedged at 8192 runs clean at 32768. We are running with this as our interim fix. (It does NOT help Mode B.) Mechanism (arithmetic exact; causation inferred): `encoder_cache_size = max(max_num_batched_tokens, max_tokens_per_mm_item=16384)`. At 8192 → 16384 holds one 11,844-token image but not two (23,688); at 32768 → holds two. Matches #40707's precondition (item 1 pinned, item 2 can't load, gap < block_size 16 → `_mamba_block_aligned_split` truncates to 0 → request skipped). Consistent with #40707, though no mamba frame appears in the stack. ## Mode B — long multi-turn text ~180k-token prefill (GDN-forward wedge) Each request is one distinct ~180k-token multi-turn conversation, no images. Wedges after ~4 completions at **both** batched 8192 and 32768: `running=1–2, waiting=10–11`, gen+prompt frozen, KV≈0.1%, ≥5 requests hit the 1200 s timeout. py-spy MainThread is **active inside the model forward** — batched-32768 run unambiguously in the GDN kernel `qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py:1532 chunk_gated_delta_rule → qwen3_5.forward → cuda_graph → execute_model`; batched-8192 run in a compiled Triton launch of the same forward. Not the scheduler. Trigger: a large **one-shot prefill** hitting the GDN chunked-prefill path — in production this is the full re-prefill after the prefix cache for a long conversation is evicted; the synthetic reproduces that single long prefill directly. (Caveat: the two dumps 3 s apart hit different compiled submodules, so the forward is grinding but never returns within 1200 s — a genuine client-side wedge, but these dumps can't fully separate an infinite hang from a pathologically-slow non-returning forward.) ## Same bug? Unknown. Both involve the GDN/mamba hybrid path, so a shared cause is plausible, but the evidence differs: Mode A = idle in scheduler, fixed by `--max-num-batched-tokens`; Mode B = active in the GDN forward, not fixed. Flagging both for maintainers who know the GDN internals; not asserting either way. ## Relation - **#40707** (OPEN) — matches Mode A; here on dense 27B / TP=1. Fix **#40709 unmerged** (not in any release through v0.27.1). - **#47738** (CLOSED, Qwen3.6-27B two images) — referenced fix **#47771 closed unmerged**. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bugfix][CI/Build] Fail closed when selected precompiled CUDA variant is unavailable
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52544.

When `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED` selects a CUDA wheel variant and metadata for that variant is unavailable, the current code falls back to the root/default wheel metadata.

As described in #xxx, this can replace the selected CUDA variant with the root/default variant without verifying CUDA compatibility. In the reproduced case, PyTorch CUDA 12.9 selected `cu129`, but the fallback wheel required `libcudart.so.13`.

This PR removes that fallback for CUDA. If metadata for the selected variant cannot be fetched, the original lookup error is propagated instead.

```text
before:

selected CUDA variant
    -> metadata lookup fails
    -> retry root/default metadata

after:

selected CUDA variant
    -> metadata lookup fails
    -> propagate the lookup failure
```

The current metadata and wheel-selection logic do not provide a way to verify that the root/default artifact is compatible with the selected CUDA variant. Given that constraint, propagating the selected-variant lookup failure is the minimal safe change for this path.

Base-commit selection is unchanged. The ROCm precompiled-wheel path is also unchanged.

## Changes

- Remove the CUDA variant -> root/default metadata fallback in `precompiled_wheel_utils.determine_wheel_url()`.
- Add regression tests for explicit and auto-detected CUDA variants.
- Run the new test in the Python-only Installation CI job.
- Update `docs/contributing/ci/nightly_builds.md` to reflect the new CUDA resolution behavior.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd tests
pytest --noconftest -q test_setup_precompiled_wheel.py
```

```bash
git diff --check
```

I also ran the same final regression test against the unmodified base commit to verify that it catches the fallback removed by this PR.

## Test Result

Patched branch:

```text
..                                                                       [100%]
2 passed
```

Same regression test against the unmodified base:

```text
FF                                                                       [100%]

Failed: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError
Failed: DID NOT RAISE RuntimeError
```

On the unmodified code, both cases call:

```text
fetch(commit, "cu129")
fetch(commit, None)
```

With this patch, they only call:

```text
fetch(commit, "cu129")
```

`git diff --check` passes.

## AI assistance

ChatGPT assisted with implementation and regression-test review, and documentation drafting. I reviewed the changes and ran the regression tests locally.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ### Summary For Python-only builds, vLLM resolves a precompiled-wheel variant before fetching wheel metadata. The [Python-only build documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/installation/gpu/) documents `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT` as selecting a variant subdirectory such as `cu129` or `cu130`. If it is not set, the CUDA variant is auto-detected from the local environment using PyTorch or `nvidia-smi`. The [nightly wheel documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/contributing/ci/nightly_builds/) describes the root index as the default variant and named subdirectories as variant-specific indices. If metadata for the selected variant cannot be fetched, [`precompiled_wheel_utils.determine_wheel_url()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6/setup.py) currently retries the root/default metadata: ```python try: wheels, repo_url = precompiled_wheel_utils.fetch_metadata_for_variant( commit, variant ) except Exception as e: logger.warning( "Failed to fetch precompiled wheel metadata for variant %s: %s", variant, e, ) try_default = True if try_default: print("Trying the default variant from remote") wheels, repo_url = precompiled_wheel_utils.fetch_metadata_for_variant( commit, None ) ``` The fallback is part of the current resolution order. The issue is that once it happens, the CUDA variant selected explicitly or detected from the local environment is no longer used to qualify the fallback wheel. The wheel filtering that follows checks the package name and target architecture: ```python if wheel.get("package_name") == "vllm" and arch in wheel.get( "platform_tag", "" ): ... ``` but does not check that the root/default artifact matches the CUDA variant selected earlier. I encountered a concrete case where PyTorch CUDA 12.9 selected `cu129`, the `cu129` metadata lookup failed, and the fallback selected a native artifact requiring CUDA 13. I propose keeping the selected CUDA variant for the rest of precompiled-wheel resolution: if its metadata cannot be fetched, propagate that lookup failure instead of retrying the root/default variant. ### Concrete reproduction I encountered this while reproducing a separate issue from the exact v0.27.1 source: ```text source: v0.27.1 6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu129 torch.version.cuda: 12.9 ``` Using the documented Python-only precompiled installation path: ```bash VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e . --torch-backend=auto ``` with neither `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT` nor `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT` set, the CUDA detection path selected: ```text cu129 ``` The Python-only build selected the following precompiled base commit: ```text f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc ``` For that commit, metadata for `cu129` was unavailable: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc/cu129/vllm/metadata.json -> 404 ``` The fallback then queried the root/default metadata: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/f5bb701fa270f5c801f1572e1478b56f292d8dfc/vllm/metadata.json -> 200 ``` The resulting path was: ```text PyTorch CUDA 12.9 -> select cu129 -> cu129 metadata unavailable -> retry root/default metadata -> select default wheel ``` ### Artifact verification I extracted `vllm/_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` from the wheel selected through the root/default fallback and inspected its ELF dependencies. The fallback artifact requires: ```text NEEDED: libcudart.so.13 ``` As a control, the published `cu129` artifact for the exact v0.27.1 commit is available at: ```text https://wheels.vllm.ai/6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac/cu129/vllm/metadata.json -> 200 ``` Its `_C_stable_libtorch.abi3.so` requires: ```text NEEDED: libcudart.so.12 ``` So in this reproduction, the resolver first selected `cu129`, then replaced that selection after the metadata failure with a root/default artifact requiring `libcudart.so.13`. The exact-v0.27.1 `cu129` artifact is only used here as a control for the native CUDA dependency of a published `cu129` wheel. I am not proposing any change to the existing base-commit selection behavior. The problematic transition happens after the base commit and CUDA variant have already been selected. ### Why the default fallback is unsafe The [nightly wheel documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/contributing/ci/nightly_builds/) treats the root index as the default variant and named subdirectories as separate variants. It also notes that the default variant can have a named alias, and that not every variant is present on every commit. A missing `cu129` index therefore does not imply that the root/default wheel is an equivalent `cu129` replacement. The current fallback nevertheless changes: ```text selected: cu129 | | metadata lookup fails v fallback: root/default | | package + architecture filtering v selected wheel ``` There is no CUDA-variant check between the selected variant and the fallback artifact. This affects explicit selection as well as auto-detection. For example, a user setting: ```text VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT=cu129 ``` can currently receive the default variant if the `cu129` metadata lookup fails. The root/default CUDA variant also cannot be inferred safely from the current `VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION`. `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_COMMIT` can select a different or historical wheel commit, and the normal Python-only path can select a base commit from `main`. The default artifact for that commit may therefore reflect a different CUDA build configuration from the one selected in the current environment. With the current metadata and wheel filtering, there is no check that makes the root/default wheel a verified replacement for an already selected CUDA variant. ### Proposed fix For CUDA, once a variant has been selected, fetch metadata only for that variant. If: ```python fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, variant) ``` fails, propagate that error instead of retrying: ```python fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, None) ``` The behavior changes from: ```text current: select cu129 -> fetch cu129 metadata -> lookup fails -> fetch root/default metadata -> select by package name / architecture ``` to: ```text proposed: select cu129 -> fetch cu129 metadata -> lookup fails -> propagate the original lookup failure ``` A fallback could be kept if the resolver had enough information to verify that the default artifact is compatible with the selected CUDA variant. That check does not exist in the current resolution path, so doing that safely would require a broader metadata or compatibility-selection change. The proposed patch instead keeps the existing variant selection intact and fails at the variant-specific lookup when that artifact is unavailable. A root/default wheel may happen to be compatible in some cases, but the current resolver cannot distinguish those cases from the incompatible case reproduced above. The existing base-commit selection is unchanged, and the ROCm precompiled-wheel path is unchanged. Regression coverage checks both CUDA selection paths: - explicit `VLLM_PRECOMPILED_WHEEL_VARIANT`; - auto-detected CUDA variant. In both cases, a failed selected-variant lookup should propagate its original error without calling `fetch_metadata_for_variant(commit, None)`. ### Current `main` The same fallback is still present on `main` at [`836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/836aac92ffdaa337083934181cb6d00b64b2a1a6). I also reproduced the path independently of the current contents of `wheels.vllm.ai` with a metadata-fetch stub: ```text fetch(commit, "cu129") -> raises fetch(commit, None) -> returns default metadata ``` On the unmodified code, both explicit and auto-detected `cu129` make both calls and return the default wheel. The regression test for the proposed behavior expects the first lookup error to propagate instead. ### Context / related work The variant-specific lookup followed by the default fallback was introduced in #29838. #32948 later added CUDA variant auto-detection while retaining that fallback. Related reports cover different paths: - #42338 reports a similar CUDA 12.9 -> CUDA 13 result through package resolver/index selection. This issue concerns the Python-only precompiled-wheel fallback after a CUDA variant has already been selected. - #49683 concerns availability of `cu129` nightly artifacts. Missing variant-specific metadata can trigger the fallback described here, but artifact availability itself is a separate problem. - PR #34139 discussed native compatibility concerns when falling back across different nightly commits. Here the wheel commit stays fixed while the selected CUDA variant is replaced by that commit's default variant. I have a patch implementing the proposed behavior with regression coverage for both explicit and auto-detected CUDA variants, and will open a draft PR shortly. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bugfix] Invalidate LazyDict cache on __setitem__
items.body:
## Purpose

`LazyDict` caches each value the first time its factory runs, but `__setitem__` only replaced the factory — it never dropped the cached value. So a key that was read before being overwritten keeps returning the old value, and the new factory is never called:

```python
d = LazyDict({"a": lambda: "first"})
d["a"]                    # "first"   (now cached in self._dict)
d["a"] = lambda: "second"
d["a"]                    # "first"   <-- stale, expected "second"
```

Overwriting *before* the first read works correctly, which is what makes this easy to miss — the broken ordering is the one that looks harmless.

```python
def __setitem__(self, key: str, value: Callable[[], _V]):
    self._factory[key] = value          # _dict[key] left holding the old value
```

## Fix

Drop the cached entry when the factory is replaced, so the next access re-evaluates.

Laziness and caching are unaffected: a factory still runs at most once per assigned value, and nothing is evaluated until accessed.

## Test Plan

Added four tests to `tests/utils_/test_collection_utils.py`:

- `test_lazy_dict_is_lazy_and_caches` — nothing evaluated until access; one factory call across two reads (guards against "fixing" this by dropping the cache entirely)
- `test_lazy_dict_setitem_replaces_cached_value` — the regression; fails on `main`
- `test_lazy_dict_setitem_before_access` — the ordering that already worked stays working
- `test_lazy_dict_new_key_and_missing_key` — assignment of a new key, `len`/`iter`, and `KeyError` for a missing key

## Test Result

```
PASS test_lazy_dict_is_lazy_and_caches
PASS test_lazy_dict_setitem_replaces_cached_value
PASS test_lazy_dict_setitem_before_access
PASS test_lazy_dict_new_key_and_missing_key
```

One disclosure on how these were run: I don't have a GPU, and `tests/conftest.py` imports `torch` at module scope, so I couldn't run the file through the repo's normal pytest entry point. I executed the four test bodies directly against `vllm/utils/collection_utils.py` instead, and confirmed the regression test fails without the one-line change. CI is the authority for the full suite.

items.title: [Bugfix] Make attention-head / TP divisibility error actionable
items.body:
Fixes #52435 (partially — complements #52446).

## Why

Serving e.g. `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with `--tensor-parallel-size 3` fails with:

```
Value error, Total number of attention heads (64) must be divisible by tensor parallel size (3).
```

The message states the constraint but not **why** or **what to do instead**, which led to the confusion in #52435 (users assume the expert-count check is the real blocker; it is not — 64 attention heads cannot be sharded across 3 TP ranks).

## Change

`ModelConfig.verify_with_parallel_config` now raises an actionable error that:
- explains tensor parallelism shards attention heads across ranks,
- lists the valid `--tensor-parallel-size` values (the divisors of the head count),
- and, when the model supports PP, suggests `--pipeline-parallel-size` (shards by layers, no head-divisibility constraint).

Example message after this change:

```
Total number of attention heads (64) must be divisible by tensor parallel size (3). Tensor parallelism shards attention heads across ranks, so only the following `--tensor-parallel-size` values are valid: [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64]. To use 3 GPUs, consider `--pipeline-parallel-size` instead, which shards the model by layers and does not require attention-head divisibility.
```

## Scope

- Pure error-message change on the validation path; no behavior, accuracy, or performance impact.
- Complements #52446 (which converts the MoE expert-count `assert` to `ValueError`); the attention-head check here was already a `ValueError`, so no exception-type change needed.
- The PP suggestion is gated on `is_pp_supported_model`, so models that don't implement `SupportsPP` are not pointed at an unsupported option.

## Tests

- `tests/config/test_head_divisibility_error.py` — 2 CPU-only tests (no model download, no GPU): asserts the actionable message (valid sizes + PP suggestion) and that a divisor TP size passes.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check`: clean on both changed files.

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Canonicalize Marlin MoE token order
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52525.

`moe_align_block_size()` guarantees expert grouping but does not guarantee the ordering of routed token IDs within an expert. For Marlin MoE, semantically equivalent within-expert orderings can select different physical block positions in the multi-threadblock split-K path and therefore follow different floating-point reduction trees.

The resulting BF16 differences are small, but they can propagate through later layers and affect autoregressive generation.

This change canonicalizes `sorted_token_ids` within each contiguous expert region before entering the Marlin MoE kernel.

The canonicalization:

- preserves expert assignment and `expert_ids`
- preserves `num_tokens_post_padded`
- keeps the inactive alignment-buffer tail from affecting the active prefix
- preserves the existing single-token decode fast path

The change is intentionally Marlin-specific because arbitrary within-expert ordering remains a valid contract for the general MoE alignment operation.

## Test Plan

- Add a focused regression test for two equivalent within-expert token orderings.
- Poison the inactive alignment-buffer tail with different arbitrary values and verify that it cannot affect the canonical active prefix.
- Validate the canonicalization helper at the routing-buffer size where the issue was isolated.
- Validate the underlying raw-vs-canonical Marlin behavior on SM120 hardware.

## Test Result

The regression case canonicalizes both equivalent layouts to the same active prefix:

`[1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 9, 0, 2, 5, 9]`

A same-forward Marlin W13 A/B experiment used identical input activations, quantized weights and scales, `expert_ids`, `num_tokens_post_padded`, top-k weights, launch parameters, and separately zeroed output/workspace buffers. The only changed input was the legal ordering of `sorted_token_ids`.

The originally isolated geometry was:

- M = 8192
- K = 4096
- N = 2048
- top_k = 6
- block_size_m = 64
- global_num_experts = 256
- local_num_experts = 128

Across 3 requests and 2 TP ranks, all 6 raw-vs-canonical comparisons produced different W13 tensors.

Observed numerical differences were small:

- max BF16 ULP distance: 4
- representative max absolute difference: 0.0078125
- representative RMS difference: ~1.50e-5
- non-finite values: 0

Canonicalizing the routed token order removed the captured W13 divergence and the downstream layer-0 divergence.

A GPU microbenchmark of the canonicalization helper on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q with a 65,280-slot routing buffer averaged 0.226 ms/call over 200 iterations.

Additional checks:

- Python source compilation: PASS
- `git diff --check`: PASS
- canonicalization regression: PASS
- DCO: PASS

## AI assistance

AI tools were used during investigation and implementation. The experiments, measurements, code changes, and validation described above were reviewed and executed by the contributor on the target hardware.

VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0

Prefix caching is OFF. All tests below are single-stream, temperature=0, max_tokens=64, identical prompt.

Failure matrix

cudagraph config | result -- | -- enforce_eager: true | Correct output, every time, across many deploys (TP16 and TP8+PP2) default (FULL_AND_PIECEWISE) | Fluent but semantically random multilingual text; host SIGSEGV in cuGraphLaunch / at::cuda::CUDAGraph::replay() on the 3rd request cudagraph_mode: PIECEWISE | No crash. DSpark speculative decoding recovers this to ~10 tok/s, still far below the graph-enabled figure. Eager is therefore not a viable workaround for latency-sensitive serving, which makes graph capture on this topology effectively blocking.

Questions

  1. Is CUDA graph capture expected to be supported for Kimi-K3 on multi-node TP without NVSwitch, where the FlashInfer fused all-reduce path is inactive and collectives fall back to NCCL over EFA? But I tried TP=8 and PP=2 the issue still persist.
  2. Are there other buffers allocated outside capture in the K3 MoE/KDA paths, analogous to the one fixed in #50386, that would be reached on the non-FlashInfer path?

Reproduction

Serve:

vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank $RANK \
  --trust-remote-code --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

#   VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=0 NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=0 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0
#   VLLM_ENABLE_K3_LATENT_MOE_TAIL_FUSION=0
# Add --enforce-eager for the known-good control run.

Single request, greedy, no concurrency:

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="<http://localhost:8000/v1>", api_key="dummy", timeout=600.0)
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="moonshotai/Kimi-K3",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "can you write me a story about a cat"}],
    max_tokens=64,
    temperature=0,
    extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking": False}},
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

With --enforce-eager this returns a coherent story on every run. Without it, the first response is already corrupted. Send the same request 3+ times to reach the segfault under the default cudagraph mode.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Fail requests the KV cache pool can never hold instead of retrying them forever
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52520.

### The symptom

On a hybrid Mamba + full-attention model with `--mamba-cache-mode align`, a request
whose length is near the KV pool ceiling is **accepted**, chunk-prefilled to ~99 % of
the pool, descheduled when the last chunk cannot be allocated — and then never
scheduled again. Zero output tokens, the whole prefill discarded, and the only
observable is `vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="capacity"} = 1`, which is
indistinguishable from a healthy server that is momentarily full. The HTTP request
never returns.

The engine boots happily into this state: `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` passes.

### The mechanism

Two bounds describe the same quantity — how many blocks one `max_model_len` request
can hold at once — and they are computed by different code that does not agree.

**Startup** sizes the pool from each spec's `max_memory_usage_bytes`
(`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:2189-2198`). For a hybrid Mamba model in align mode
that is `cdiv(max_model_len, block_size)` blocks for the attention group plus
`2 + num_speculative_blocks` for the Mamba group
(`vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:687-696`). It compares that against **all** the
blocks the pool will have. But `BlockPool` permanently reserves one block as the null
block (`vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py:188-191`), so only `num_blocks - 1` are ever
available to a request. A pool built at exactly the startup minimum is one usable
block short of one `max_model_len` request, and startup does not notice.

**Runtime admission** (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py:475-491`, reached with
`scheduler_reserve_full_isl` — default `True`) asks the coordinator for the same
quantity, but through the per-step allocators. For the Mamba align group that path
returns `1 + num_speculative_blocks` on a first prefill
(`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py:1529-1540`), one block below the peak
the spec itself states, because a later step allocates the next state block before
`remove_skipped_blocks` retires the one from two steps ago. So admission asks for one
block *less* than the pool is short by, and admits.

The request then chunk-prefills until the final chunk needs the block that does not
exist. It is the only running request, so it preempts itself
(`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:676-688`): `num_computed_tokens` back to 0, all
blocks freed, requeued. On the next step the same gate now also has to count the
blocks the discarded prefill left in the prefix cache as evictable, so it refuses —
and keeps refusing. The request is stuck, and the prefill is gone.

Measured on unmodified `main` at `4d2a68d64d9e05921ed5c4099146e768a92d71d5`, CPU only,
no model weights: hybrid full-attention + Mamba(align), `block_size=16`,
`max_model_len=1024`, `num_speculative_blocks=3`, `max_num_batched_tokens=256`. The
startup bound is `cdiv(1024,16)=64 + (2+3)=5 = 69` blocks, and
`get_kv_cache_configs` accepts a 69-block pool:

```text
pool of 69 blocks: startup check accepts=True (num_blocks=69)
  pool=69 blocks, free at start=68 (one block is BlockPool's null block)
    step   0 scheduled=  256 computed=  256 free= 48 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   1 scheduled=  256 computed=  512 free= 31 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   2 scheduled=  256 computed=  768 free= 15 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   3 scheduled=  240 computed= 1008 free=  0 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   4 scheduled=    0 computed=    0 free= 68 status=PREEMPTED preemptions=1
    step   5 scheduled=    0 computed=    0 free= 68 status=PREEMPTED preemptions=1
    ... 19 more identical steps ...
  VERDICT prompt=1023: finished=False computed=0 preemptions=1 status=PREEMPTED

pool of 70 blocks: startup check accepts=True (num_blocks=70)
    step   3 scheduled=  240 computed= 1008 free=  1 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
    step   4 scheduled=   15 computed= 1023 free=  0 status=RUNNING preemptions=0
  VERDICT prompt=1023: finished=False computed=1023 preemptions=0 status=RUNNING
```

One block of headroom is the entire difference. Note that the prefill dies at exactly
1008 tokens, which is `(69 - 1 - 5) * 16` — the sequence length the pool can actually
serve.

### The fix

One function computes the bound, and it is the function the startup error message
already uses:

- `max_servable_num_tokens(vllm_config, kv_cache_groups, num_blocks)` in
  `kv_cache_utils.py` — the longest sequence a pool of `num_blocks` blocks can hold
  for one request. It is `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` (the helper behind
  "the estimated maximum model length" that `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` prints)
  evaluated against `num_blocks - 1` blocks, i.e. against the capacity `BlockPool`
  will actually hand out. It returns `None` for group layouts that cannot be priced
  per block — exactly the layouts whose pool was not sized per block either — so it
  never invents a bound the startup check did not apply.
- `Scheduler` evaluates it once at construction. When it is below `max_model_len` the
  configuration cannot serve its own window, which is logged at `ERROR` with the
  number the operator needs. A request past the bound can never be scheduled at any
  future time, however much drains, so `add_request` fails it immediately instead of
  queueing it: no prefill is spent, nothing is preempted, and the client gets a
  terminal response rather than a request that never returns.

So there is one bound with two call sites, which is the point:
`_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups` is called by the startup check
(`kv_cache_utils.py:2234`, via `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory`) and now by
`max_servable_num_tokens`, which is what the scheduler admits against. Neither side
can grow its own formula without the other seeing it.

The failure uses `RequestStatus.FINISHED_IGNORED`, which `vllm/v1/request.py` already
documents as the status for "requests whose prompt lengths are longer than the
model's length cap", mapping to `finish_reason="length"`. `FinishReason.ERROR` is
documented as a *retryable* internal error always converted to a 500, which is the
wrong contract here. Returning a literal 400 would mean exposing the pool-derived
bound to `input_processor._validate_prompt_len`, where `max_model_len` is validated;
happy to do that in a follow-up if maintainers prefer it — it is a frontend/engine-core
plumbing change and I kept it out of this PR.

Behaviour is unchanged whenever the pool covers `max_model_len`, which is every
correctly-sized deployment: the bound is then `>= max_model_len`, `_is_unservable`
short-circuits on the first comparison, and nothing is rejected. The 70-block row
above is byte-for-byte identical before and after.

### Relationship to #47272 — scoped around it, not a duplicate

I read #47272 ("Reserve the KV null block when validating `max_model_len`") before
writing any code, and this PR is deliberately scoped around it.

- **#47272 owns the capacity side.** It subtracts one block from the memory the
  startup check validates against, so a pool that cannot serve `max_model_len` is
  refused at boot with the existing message naming the estimated maximum model
  length. That is the right place for it and this PR does not touch that code path.
  Applied to the reproduction above, #47272 makes the 69-block pool illegal at
  startup — which is a better outcome than anything the scheduler can do, and is why
  I am not proposing an alternative to it.
- **This PR owns the request side.** It makes the runtime bound the same function as
  the startup bound, and gives the engine an answer for a request it cannot serve
  other than retrying it. That is needed independently of #47272, because the
  scheduler currently has *no* concept of "this request can never be scheduled": it
  only distinguishes "not now". If #47272 lands, this PR's check becomes dormant on
  correctly-sized pools (bound `>= max_model_len`) and remains the backstop for the
  paths #47272 does not cover — notably `_auto_fit_max_model_len`, which runs before
  #47272's reservation and can still land on the boundary.
- The two compose cleanly and neither subsumes the other. **Please do not merge this
  instead of #47272.**

Other prior art I checked: **#40946** (merged) is the design precedent — it fixed the
same class of defect (startup pool sizing and runtime admission using different
formulas) for SWA/chunked-local by putting the bound in one method called from both
sites, and this PR follows that shape. **#35541** (closed not-planned/stale) asked for
"abort requests that can never fit in the KV cache block pool with a clear error
rather than hanging indefinitely" — this is that, for the mechanism above. **#40384**
is why the numbers here are stated in blocks and tokens rather than inverted from the
`GPU KV cache size` log line, which on a hybrid model is
`num_blocks // len(kv_cache_groups) * min_block_size`.

### Scope of the claim

The field trace in #52520 came from a **downstream fork build** on a hybrid Qwen3.5
model (261,794-token request, `--enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align`, MTP
depth 3, pool within ~1 % of the window; 63 full re-prefills over 656 s with zero
output tokens). The mechanism above is upstream code, and everything in this PR is
demonstrated on **stock `main` at `4d2a68d64d9e05921ed5c4099146e768a92d71d5`** by the
CPU-only unit test below — no GPU, no model weights, no fork code involved.

One part of the original report I could **not** reproduce on `main` and am therefore
not claiming: `vllm:num_preemptions_total` staying at `0.0` across the re-prefills.
On `main` the self-preemption path does increment `request.num_preemptions` and record
`EngineCoreEventType.PREEMPTED`, which `IterationStats` counts into
`vllm:num_preemptions_total`. So there is no accounting fix here, and I am not filing
one. (With this PR the point is moot for this defect: nothing is preempted, because
nothing is admitted, and the operator gets two `ERROR` lines naming the limit.)

### The decode case, added in the second commit

Review raised it and I measured it on the same stock-`main` harness: the admission
gate bounds a request on `num_tokens + 1`, but a generate request grows to
`prompt + max_tokens`. With `block_size` 16, `max_model_len` 1024 and the 69-block
pool above (`max_servable_num_tokens` 1008), `prompt=1000, max_tokens=24` clears the
frontend (`1000 + 24 <= 1024`, `vllm/renderers/params.py:210,442`) and clears
admission (`1000 + 1 <= 1008`), and then reaches 1009 tokens at output token 9. On
`main` it is preempted there, is now too long to re-prefill, and the next **3987
scheduler steps schedule zero tokens, produce no output and leave all 68 blocks
free** — the same terminal state as the prefill case, reached through decode.

Bounding admission on `num_tokens + max_tokens` would close it, but would refuse
requests that stop well before the wall: on that same pool, `max_tokens=8` runs to
completion in 12 steps. So the ceiling is applied where it belongs, as a length cap:
`check_stop` takes `max_servable_num_tokens` instead of `max_model_len`. Those are
equal on every pool that covers its window — `_estimate_max_model_len_from_groups`
searches with `right = original_max` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:1960`), and the
scheduler falls back to `max_model_len` when there is no per-block bound — so the
common path is unchanged. Where they differ the request stops on the ceiling and
returns its tokens with `finish_reason: length`, exactly as if `max_model_len` had
been set to what the pool can serve.

That is one bound with three call sites: startup sizing, admission, and the length
cap.

The spec-decode lookahead can also reach past the ceiling, because the running path
asks for `1 + len(spec_token_ids)` slots. Measured on stock `main` with drafts
injected: it preempts twice and then finishes, because preemption clears
`spec_token_ids` and the retry decodes into the cap. Bounded and self-correcting, so
`sched/scheduler.py:605` is left alone.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py
# surrounding suite, unchanged behaviour:
pytest tests/v1/core/
```

`tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py` is CPU-only
(`pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test`), built the same way as
`tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py`: a real `Scheduler` over a hand-built
hybrid `KVCacheConfig`, driven with `schedule()` / `update_from_output()`. No model
weights, no GPU. Seven cases:

1. `test_max_servable_num_tokens_reserves_the_null_block` — the bound is
   `(69 - 1 - 5) * 16 = 1008` at the startup minimum, and `>= max_model_len` with one
   block of headroom.
2. `test_unservable_request_is_failed_not_prefilled_and_retried` — the regression
   test. A 1023-token request on the 69-block pool: nothing is scheduled, it is
   finished as `FINISHED_IGNORED`, `num_computed_tokens == 0`,
   `num_preemptions == 0`, and no unfinished request is left behind.
3. `test_request_at_the_bound_is_failed_because_it_needs_an_output_slot` — the bound
   is a sequence length, so a prompt of exactly 1008 is already too long (it was the
   one length that prefilled fully on `main` and then stalled on its first decode
   step).
4. `test_servable_request_at_the_same_pool_still_runs` — 1007 tokens on the *same*
   69-block pool prefills fully, decodes, and finishes. The bound must not
   over-reject.
5. `test_pool_with_headroom_serves_the_whole_window` — 1023 tokens on a 70-block pool
   behaves exactly as before this PR.
6. `test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode` — the decode
   regression test. `prompt=1000, max_tokens=24` on the 69-block pool clears both
   length checks, then must finish `FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED` at 1008 tokens with
   `num_preemptions == 0` and nothing left unfinished.
7. `test_generation_is_not_capped_when_the_pool_covers_the_window` — the same request
   with one block of headroom must still produce all 24 tokens, so the length cap
   cannot silently truncate generation on the common path.

## Test Result

The new file, checked out on top of unmodified `main` at `4d2a68d6` (the fix reverted,
the test kept), fails:

```text
$ git checkout HEAD -- vllm/ && pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q
FAILED test_max_servable_num_tokens_reserves_the_null_block
  - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens'
FAILED test_unservable_request_is_failed_not_prefilled_and_retried
  - AssertionError: assert not {'0': 256}
FAILED test_request_at_the_bound_is_failed_because_it_needs_an_output_slot
  - AssertionError: assert not {'0': 256}
FAILED test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode
  - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens'
FAILED test_generation_is_not_capped_when_the_pool_covers_the_window
  - AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'max_servable_num_tokens'
5 failed, 2 passed, 14 warnings in 4.81s
```

`{'0': 256}` is `main` admitting the unservable request and scheduling the first
256-token prefill chunk of the sequence it will then throw away. The two that pass
before and after are the two "must still work" directions — they are there to catch
over-rejection and over-capping, and they must never have gone red.

Reverting only the one-line length cap and keeping everything else isolates the
decode case:

```text
$ sed -i 's/self.max_servable_num_tokens)/self.max_model_len)/' <the check_stop call>
$ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q
FAILED test_generation_stops_at_the_bound_instead_of_stalling_mid_decode
  - assert <RequestStatus.PREEMPTED: 6> == <RequestStatus.FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED: 8>
1 failed, 6 passed, 14 warnings in 4.92s
```

With the fix:

```text
$ pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_pool_unservable_requests.py -q
.......                                                                  [100%]
7 passed, 14 warnings in 4.71s
```

Surrounding suite, same command on `4d2a68d6` and on this branch:

```text
main @ 4d2a68d6 : 2 failed, 495 passed, 2 errors in 348.75s
this branch     : 2 failed, 502 passed, 2 errors in 375.92s
```

The same two failures and the same two setup errors occur on both, all environmental
in my CPU-only sandbox and unrelated to this change: failures in
`test_scheduler.py::test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders`
and `test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e.py::test_reset_prefix_cache_e2e`, and setup errors on
`test_concurrent_partial_prefill` and `test_prefix_cache_stats_is_recorded` — all four
need a GPU-backed engine core. The +7 are the new tests.

Two existing tests build a `Scheduler` with `object.__new__` and set its attributes by
hand; they each gain one line for the new `unservable_reqs` set and one for
`max_servable_num_tokens`
(`tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`, `tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py`).

Lint gates on the changed files:

```text
$ ruff check <changed files>          # 0.14.0, as pinned in .pre-commit-config.yaml
All checks passed!

(clean)
```

items.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Only echo the assistant turn in batched chat completions
items.body:
## Purpose

In the batched chat completion path, `echo=true` prepends `conversation[-1]["content"]` to the model's answer without checking the role of that last message. With the default `add_generation_prompt=true`, the last conversation message is the **user's prompt**, so the user's own prompt is prepended to the assistant's response:

```
"USER PROMPTASSISTANT ANSWER"   # expected: "ASSISTANT ANSWER"
```

The non-batched path in `vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py` already guards against this with an extra clause. `role` is computed identically in both files, so this PR adds the same clause to the batched path:

```python
and conversation[-1].get("role") == role
```

This restores parity between the two paths: a trailing *user* turn is no longer echoed, while a genuine assistant prefix (`continue_final_message=true`) still is.

### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

I searched open PRs and issues for `batch_serving`, `batch echo`, `echo assistant role conversation` and `batched chat completions echo`; nothing open touches this code path. The nearby batch-serving PRs are unrelated (#42105 reasoning-parser, stale; #50042 / #50027 stream and tools rejection).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_batched_chat_completions.py -v -k echo
pre-commit run --all-files
```

Two regression tests were added to the designated file. They construct `OpenAIServingChatBatch` via `__new__` and await the real `chat_completion_full_generator_batch` with stub generators, so they exercise the production echo-assembly code directly without requiring an engine — which also means they run in seconds and need no GPU.

## Test Result

```
# before the fix
FAILED test_batched_echo_does_not_prepend_user_prompt
E   AssertionError: assert 'USER PROMPTASSISTANT ANSWER' == 'ASSISTANT ANSWER'
1 failed, 1 passed

# after the fix
2 passed
```

`test_batched_echo_prepends_matching_assistant_prefix` passes both before and after, confirming the legitimate `continue_final_message` echo path is unchanged.

The five pre-existing e2e tests in this file require `RemoteOpenAIServer` and a GPU, so I could not execute them locally; they are untouched by this change. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the modified files.

Model evals were not run: this change removes text that should never have been in the response and does not affect generation itself.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance (noted in the commit trailer per AGENTS.md). I reviewed every changed line, compared the batched path against the non-batched sibling to confirm the fix matches its formatting and semantics, and ran the tests above.
